title: Creme Caramel
description: A French classic — silky custard topped with a thin layer of amber caramel. Made possible with the LG Kitchen collection.

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 160°C (140°C fan-forced) on top and bottom heat. Line a roasting tray with a clean tea towel.
Place 165 g of the caster sugar and 125 ml water in a medium heavy-based saucepan. Place pan on medium heat and cook, stirring, until sugar dissolves without boiling.

Bring to the boil without stirring until mixture turns a deep amber caramel colour. Remove from heat and allow bubbles to subside. Carefully pour caramel into a deep 20cm round cake pan, tilting to coat the base evenly.
In a separate saucepan, bring thickened cream and milk almost to the boil over medium heat.
Meanwhile, in a large heatproof bowl, whisk eggs, vanilla extract, and the remaining 75 g of caster sugar until well combined.
Whisking continuously, slowly pour the hot cream and milk mixture into the egg mixture. Strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into the cake pan over the set caramel.
Place the cake pan in the prepared roasting tray. Fill a kettle or saucepan with water and bring just to the boil.
Place roasting tray in the oven. Carefully pour enough boiling water into the tray to come halfway up the side of the cake pan.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until the custard is set but still has a slight wobble in the centre.
Remove the cake pan from the roasting tray. Allow to cool completely, then cover and refrigerate overnight.
To serve, run a thin knife around the edge of the pan. Invert onto a deep-sided serving plate. The caramel will form a golden sauce. Serve with fresh raspberries if desired.

notes.title: Make-Ahead
notes.content: Crème caramel needs to be refrigerated overnight to set properly. Start this recipe a day before serving.

notes.title: Caramel Colour
notes.content: Do not use a saucepan with a dark interior when making caramel — it will be very hard to gauge the depth of colour. The caramel will continue to darken slightly off the heat, so remove it just before it reaches your desired colour.

notes.title: Water Bath
notes.content: The water bath (bain-marie) ensures gentle, even cooking. The tea towel in the roasting tray prevents the cake pan from sliding and helps distribute heat evenly.

notes.title: Straining is Essential
notes.content: Straining the custard removes any bits of cooked egg and ensures a perfectly smooth, silky texture.
